findings.reason: a node following the citation derives the trailing rate from a transition log rather than a reading series and ships a field that is null in the case the section was written for, so the source it names changes what the node builds and whether the section's purpose is met.
findings.text: §46 writes that `window_rate_pct_per_hour` "is read from the group's stored readings (`record_checks`, `reckon/budget.py:1503`) plus the current reading", but `record_checks` persists through `ledger.record_hold_checks`, whose own contract is that at most one hold is open per backend and rechecking a backend while it remains held preserves one record for a continuous hold window (`reckon/ledger.py:4016-4018`) — the store keeps one record per hold transition, not a series of readings, so the field's own requirement ("null when fewer than two readings lie at least 30 minutes apart") would be unmet for every lane that is not being held, which is the lane §46 exists to show Jev; the collectors that do hold a reading series are `_readings` ("Collect every recorded budget block for a project, from both homes", `reckon/budget.py:569`) and the published headroom document read by `budget_lift.published_readings` (`reckon/crew/budget_lift.py:194`)

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every file and symbol anchor resolves, with two stale line offsets that still resolve by the symbol named beside them; all counts were read in the assigned worktree at `8793a6ca2`. Exact: `record_checks` `reckon/budget.py:1503`, `_credit_lift_verdict` `reckon/budget.py:1269`, `decide` `reckon/budget.py:1344`, `_reserved_lane_exclusion` `reckon/crew/picker/snapshot.py:1080`, `effective_budget` `reckon/crew/budget_lift.py:553`, `utilisation_ceiling_pct` comparison `reckon/crew/picker/snapshot.py:1380-1381`, `_hold_marker` `reckon/crew/budget_lift.py:872`. Stale: §46 cites `_burn_floor_reason` at `reckon/budget.py:1094`, where 1094 is a `return (` inside `_is_known` and the definition is at 1124; §47 cites the raw comparison at `reckon/crew/picker/snapshot.py:1315`, where 1315 is a closing paren. Both name the symbol in the same sentence, so a node finds each in one grep and the drifted offsets assert nothing false about behaviour. §46's claim that a picker row carries `utilisation_pct`, `days_to_reset`, `pace_allowance` and `burn_multiple` is confirmed field-for-field on `Candidate` (`reckon/crew/picker/types.py:25-41`), and its "null in a window's first 5%" matches `BURN_ELAPSED_FRACTION_FLOOR = 0.05` (`reckon/budget.py:105`). The schema files §46 and §48 write exist, including `docs/_shared/flight.schema.json` and the `routing:` block `budget_period_hours` joins (`reckon/schema/flight.yaml:324`).
rubric_items.done_when: pass — each of the three sections pairs its measure with a negative control whose mutation its assertions would falsify, each applied alone under a short-summary pytest. §46's whole-window-average mutation fails the 2%-elapsed case (a whole-window average at 2% elapsed reads about 1000 points/hour against the asserted 8) and the reserve omission fails the pool case (9,000 against 8,000). §47's restored raw comparison fails cases 1 and 4 (the configured `utilisation_ceiling_pct` is 100, so a 100% window is excluded and a 93% lane is offered where the case requires it excluded), and its retained window term fails case 1. §48's applied pace hold fails case 1 and its kept reserves fail case 2 (92% against the asserted 100%). Each done-when also names a base arm at the dispatched base with the manifest's `baseline_suite`, and a ruff delta on the staged paths.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — both arms' logs go in the crew run directory, with `baseline_suite` naming the base log and its failure ids, and the remaining artifact is the node's evidence fragment. Neither is a scratchpad or a node-local temporary path, and both survive the run.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the introduced names state the mechanism and carry no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag: `window_rate_pct_per_hour`, `window_even_share_pct`, `credit_pool_remaining`, `credit_rate_per_hour`, `credit_even_share`, `runway_hours`, `burn`, and the declaration value `pace: advisory`. No changelog prose or tracker reference appears in the three sections or their followups.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §47's root cause and mechanism both hold (the picker's raw comparison at `reckon/crew/picker/snapshot.py:1380-1381` reads the configured ceiling through `budget.policy`, while dispatch's fresh stop is the ceiling less the two reserves at `reckon/budget.py:249-254`, so reading the lift-aware verdict through `effective_budget` is the right repair); §48's premise also holds (`effective_budget` zeroes all three reserves and carries the pace-hold marker under a lift, `reckon/crew/budget_lift.py:620-632`). §46 is where the mechanism does not produce its own measure.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §46 delivers one thing (a `burn` block derived once in `reckon/budget.py` and rendered by the picker, with no figure computed in the picker); §47 one thing (the picker excludes a lane exactly when a dispatch of the pick's purpose would be held); §48 one thing (a group may declare its pace advisory). The host-flight reserve (§47) and `codex-sub` advisory (§48) are labelled coordinator steps after landing, not node deliverables.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — the `plan-section-depends-on` meta records `s46:[lane-and-model-routing#s47]` and `s48:[lane-and-model-routing#s46]`, matching the file-overlap order the sections state for themselves (§47 "so this section is dispatched first and §46 after it merges", §48 "so this section is dispatched after §46 merges", both over `reckon/crew/picker/snapshot.py` and `reckon/budget.py`); §47 needs no predecessor and declares none. `picker_reserved_lanes`, the host-flight step §47 asks the coordinator for, resolves as `reckon/flight.py:99` and is a real flight key.
